resources.string: Pair FSVoip with an extension of your phone system. Then you call from this phone with your company\'s number.
In the portal, open Telephony, choose your extension and tap Pair FSVoip.
Scan the QR code with this phone, or tap the pairing link.
Done: your extension is in the app and you can call.
The code is valid for 10 minutes and works once.
Point the camera at the QR code in the portal. Pairing only starts when you confirm it.
FSVoip asks for camera access to scan the QR code.
FSVoip may not use the camera. Allow it in Settings, or paste the pairing link below.
No camera is available. Paste the pairing link below.
This phone will be paired with an extension of your phone system. If FSVoip on another phone uses that extension, it stops working there.
Your extension gets a new password that is stored on this phone only.
Your extension is in FSVoip. You can call as soon as its light is green.
This code has expired or was already used. Create a new code in the portal and scan it.
Too many attempts from this network. Try again in fifteen minutes.
The phone system is not responding right now. The code was not used: try again shortly.
No internet connection. Check your connection and try again.
This pairing was revoked. Pair the extension again from the portal.
The phone could not store the details securely. Unlock the phone and try again.
The other side put you on hold
This number cannot be called. Use digits only, optionally with + at the start.
Pair an extension first to make calls.
This extension is not connected to the phone system yet. Wait until its light is green.
You are already on a call.
The call could not start. Try again.
Calls made with FSVoip show up here. They stay on this phone.
Clear all recent calls on this phone?
Green: connected to the phone system. Orange: connecting. Red: there is a problem.
This extension is used unless you choose another one. On the call screen you can pick a different extension per call.
Leave empty to use the name from the portal: %1$s.
An incoming call then shows, for example, “Bakery Smit → %1$s”.
Unpairing removes this extension from this phone. The extension itself stays on your phone system.
You can then no longer call or be called with this extension on this phone.
The phone system cannot be reached right now. You can remove the extension from this phone only; the pairing then stays in the portal until you remove it there.
The pairing of %1$s was revoked. The extension was removed from this phone.
This is not an FSVoip pairing code.
The pairing link has no code.
The pairing code is not valid. Create a new code in the portal.

Off: an incoming call only shows as a notification. Tap to turn it on.
On: an incoming call fills the screen, also when the phone is locked.
Off: you do not see incoming calls while the app is closed. Tap to allow notifications.
Some phones (Samsung, Xiaomi, Huawei, OnePlus) stop apps in the background. Turn battery saving off for FSVoip so you do not miss calls.
FSVoip may run in the background.
Shows the name of a caller from the contacts on this phone. They stay on the phone.
This build does not receive calls while the app is closed (push is not set up).

AndroidX and Jetpack Compose, Kotlin and kotlinx (Apache-2.0), OkHttp (Apache-2.0), AndroidX Media3 / ExoPlayer (Apache-2.0), ZXing and zxing-android-embedded (Apache-2.0) and Firebase Cloud Messaging (Apache-2.0). See NOTICE in the source code.
FSVoip may not use the microphone. Allow it in Settings, otherwise the other side cannot hear you.

Callers can leave a message when you do not answer.
All calls for this device go to the destination you choose, for example your mobile.
Without a choice, what is shown above happens.
Your phone rings for an incoming call.
Do not disturb is on: incoming calls do not reach your extension.
Choose the number you call with

When you do not answer, these numbers are called one after the other. At most 10 steps.

No connection. This is the last known state; pull down to reload.
Unlock with your fingerprint, face or screen lock to set up the PBX.
Open the settings of your PBX
First set a screen lock on this phone (Settings > Security). Then you can set up the PBX here.
You are no longer an admin. The phone system settings are hidden.

Set up the phone system of this phone: forwarding, ring groups and opening hours. Admins only.
Your change is saved. Pull down to refresh.
The phone system is busy with another change. Try again shortly.
The default: opening hours first, then who answers.
Choose where callers of this number go first.
For example your mobile number. Some numbers can be blocked.
Choose how long we wait before this number is called, and how long it rings.
Tap Edit at the top right to change the order.
Set your opening hours in the portal. Then you can adjust them here.
Holidays and temporarily closed days work like outside opening hours.
On these days callers get the same as outside opening hours. You can open the days again below.
You can set at most %1$d own days.
You can close at most %1$d own days. There is room for %2$d more; open older days again first.

As soon as a phone number is connected to your phone system, you set it up here.

Decide when you can be reached and what happens outside those hours.
Without opening hours you can always be reached on this number.
Tap a day to change its hours. Green is open.
Opens the hours of this day.
Up to four time slots a day. 24:00 means until midnight.
The end is not after the start
